questions.q: In the Section 1 security tests, what should happen when Derek Oyelaran logs in and views Opportunities?
options: He sees only his own records, with no rollup from his team
He sees Tom Baptiste's and Jordan Kessler's records, but not Priya Nair's
He sees nothing, since Sales Managers have no Opportunity access
He sees every Opportunity in the org
questions.explain: Role hierarchy rolls access up to Oyelaran for his direct reports (Baptiste and Kessler) but not for Nair, whose role reports directly to Monica Reyes instead.

questions.q: Why does Section 1 include a negative test -- Tom Baptiste attempting to open a Service Contract?
options: Because Service Contract has no OWD setting
Negative tests are only needed for Flows, not security
To confirm access is correctly blocked where it should be, not just that access correctly works where it should
Because Baptiste's profile is being retired
questions.explain: A full test plan confirms both that the right people CAN see records and that the wrong people correctly CANNOT -- a negative test catches an overly permissive profile a positive-only test plan would miss.

questions.q: What does the Section 2 "no-change run" of the Screen Flow test for?
options: That the Flow deletes the Installation Project if nothing changes
That the Flow requires at least one field to be filled in before it can run
That running the Flow without changing anything doesn't unintentionally overwrite or blank out existing field values
That the Flow automatically creates a Service Contract
questions.explain: This guards against a common Flow bug: an Update Records element overwriting a field with a blank value when the user didn't actually intend to change it.

questions.q: Why does Section 3 test each validation rule with both a failing case and a passing case?
options: Salesforce requires every validation rule to be tested twice before activation
Only the failing case actually matters for testing
To confirm the rule correctly blocks bad data AND correctly allows good data through once the problem is fixed, rather than being too strict or too loose
Passing cases are only relevant for Flows, not validation rules
questions.explain: Testing only the failing case wouldn't catch a rule written so strictly that it also blocks legitimate, corrected data -- testing both confirms the rule fires exactly when it should.

questions.q: What does the Section 4 "below threshold" approval process test confirm?
options: That the record locks regardless of discount size
That Approval_Status__c is set to Rejected automatically
That Monica Reyes is notified even for small discounts
That a discount below the entry criteria doesn't trigger the approval process at all
questions.explain: With Discount Percent at 10 (below the 15% entry criteria), the approval process's criteria aren't met, so submission has no effect -- confirming the threshold is correctly enforced.
